protections: A peer-declared 4-byte frame length is validated before allocation: KafkaProtocol._validate_frame_size rejects nbytes < 0 or nbytes > _max_frame_size and raises InvalidReceiveError (kafka/protocol/parser.py:143-145), called at kafka/protocol/parser.py:114-117 immediately before KafkaBytes(nbytes); the bound is inclusive and 0 is accepted, which the tests pin (test/protocol/test_parser.py:286-306).

Every runtime KafkaProtocol is built with the configured cap: KafkaConnection.connection_made passes config['receive_message_max_bytes'] (kafka/net/connection.py:268-271) and the connection is created from the manager's merged config (kafka/net/manager.py:275), so with the single runtime construction site (kafka/protocol/parser.py:117) there is no unguarded parser instance in the client stack.

Client defaults set that cap to 1 MB: kafka/net/connection.py:27, kafka/net/manager.py:29, kafka/consumer/group.py:325, kafka/producer/kafka.py:415, kafka/admin/client.py:168, documented as 'Used to avoid OOM when decoding malformed network message header' (kafka/consumer/group.py:179-181).
The parser's own default when constructed directly is 100000000 (100 MB) (kafka/protocol/parser.py:29, docstring kafka/protocol/parser.py:23-24).

There is NO bound on the SCRAM server-first parameters: the base64 salt is decoded as-is (kafka/sasl/scram.py:101) and the iteration count is passed straight to pbkdf2_hmac (kafka/sasl/scram.py:102, 115-118), reached from the connection's SASL loop (kafka/net/connection.py:431-432, 460).

There is NO bound on decompressed record-batch output: gzip, snappy, lz4 and zstd decoders return whatever the stream expands to (kafka/codec.py:94-103, 200-222, 250-256, 319-323) even though an unused constant ZSTD_MAX_OUTPUT_SIZE exists (kafka/codec.py:9), and callers assign the result directly (kafka/record/default_records.py:240-250, kafka/record/legacy_records.py:204-213, 268).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: SASL only talks to the broker the operator chose to authenticate to, the SCRAM token arrives inside a frame the parser already caps (kafka/protocol/parser.py:144), and the report is about 'peer-declared length' - so a solver who finds the frame check closed can call the DoS story handled and never open kafka/sasl/scram.py.

The salt sits on the line above the iteration count and looks harmless: real salts are 16-64 bytes and the base64 blob is already inside a capped frame, so a length check looks redundant - and the published iteration cap at kafka/sasl/scram.py:102 leaves this line untouched.

The check exists and is configurable: 1 MB is a deliberate, documented client default (kafka/consumer/group.py:179-181) and a direct KafkaProtocol user gets the documented 100 MB parser default (kafka/protocol/parser.py:29), so nothing is 'missing' and the obvious move is to leave the value alone.

No runtime caller decodes framed: grep over kafka/ finds only the encode path (kafka/protocol/parser.py:61) and framed decode appears only in tests (test/protocol/metadata/test_api_versions.py:70, test/protocol/old/test_old_api_versions.py:75); kafka.protocol.old is imported only by kafka/benchmarks/protocol_old_vs_new.py, and both decoders read the size without allocating from it, so there is nothing to exploit here.

This is not a peer-declared length, so it is outside the advisory's mechanism; the compressed input is already bounded by the frame cap (kafka/protocol/parser.py:144) and upstream Kafka clients do not cap decompressed size either - so a solver can reasonably say the allocation is already bounded.

masking: T5's decompression amplification only becomes material at scale once T3's frame cap is reconciled with the multi-megabyte Fetch responses the consumer already asks for (kafka/consumer/group.py:302 vs kafka/consumer/group.py:325): raising the cap to keep large Fetch working enlarges the compressed input a hostile broker can expand (kafka/codec.py:319-323).

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T3 (tighten the effective frame cap to a small fixed value, or lower the parser's 100 MB default at kafka/protocol/parser.py:29) contradicts the coupled must-keep-working value that the client itself requests up to 52,428,800 bytes of Fetch data (kafka/consumer/group.py:302) with a 1,048,576-byte per-partition allowance (kafka/consumer/group.py:303); the natural fix for T5 (cap decompressed output in kafka/codec.py) must then be sized against that larger frame cap, and a cap tight enough to stop amplification breaks legitimately compressed batches (test/test_codec.py:126-133).

fairness_risks: Legit frames above the client cap exist by design: fetch_max_bytes defaults to 52428800 and max_partition_fetch_bytes to 1048576 (kafka/consumer/group.py:302-303) while receive_message_max_bytes defaults to 1000000 (kafka/consumer/group.py:325), and the fetch docstring states an oversized first message is still returned so the consumer can make progress (kafka/consumer/group.py:86-93). A rule that hardcodes a small frame cap or rejects frames >= 1 MB breaks normal consuming.

Boundary shapes must stay accepted: a frame exactly at the maximum is valid, a zero-length frame is valid, and the length header arriving split across TCP reads must not be rejected before all 4 header bytes exist (test/protocol/test_parser.py:286-306, kafka/protocol/parser.py:108-118).

Legit SCRAM parameters: RFC/Kafka brokers normally use 4096-16384 iterations and 16-64 byte salts, and some deployments use much higher counts; a cap set at the expected value, a strict regex on the integer, or a small salt-length limit rejects valid clusters.

Legit compressed record batches expand far beyond their compressed size and multi-frame zstd payloads must decode (test/test_codec.py:126-133); a decompression limit that truncates, raises on multi-frame input, or is set near the compressed size breaks real consumers.

A refused input shape a legitimate use needs: the server-first message is parsed with a naive split on ',' and dict(pair.split('=', 1)) (kafka/sasl/scram.py:94), so strictness added there can reject conforming servers whose base64 salt carries padding or whose 'i' has leading whitespace/zeros.

design.why: Four traps over four independent guard groups. T1/T2 share one parse in ScramClient.process_server_first_message (kafka/sasl/scram.py:92-103) but are two different resources (blocking pbkdf2 work factor vs salt allocation) and the published iteration cap at kafka/sasl/scram.py:102 does not close the salt at :101, so a solver can half-fix the block and still pass a naive self-check. T1 is the deepseek-type trap: the protection is absent, the peer is the broker the client chose, and the reported 'peer-declared length' frame check is verifiably closed at the pin (kafka/protocol/parser.py:143-145, kafka/net/connection.py:268-271, test/protocol/test_parser.py:272-306) - the strongest possible reason to stop. T2 and T3 are the mimo-type traps: both are coupled values, so over-hardening is the likely failure - a salt cap that rejects conforming salts, or a frame cap tightened to 1 MB that breaks the client's own 50 MB Fetch request (kafka/consumer/group.py:302 vs :325). T5 is a second deepseek-type (absent protection plus 'it is not a declared length, so out of scope'), and its severity is coupled to T3. T4 is held in reserve as a fifth, pure reason-to-dismiss group (a second framed decoder that discards the declared size but is never reached at runtime: kafka/protocol/api_message.py:254-255, kafka/protocol/old/api.py:131-132, only tests pass framed=True). This beats a frame-size-only design, which the pinned code has already fixed and whose tests are in-tree.
